findings.detail: The framework projects cumulative deficits totalling £38m over 5 years. Table 5 shows deficits every year from 2026/27–2029/30, with no earmarked reserves drawn to bridge them. The authority must find savings equivalent to 3.9–4.1% of budget annually.
findings.matters: An integration authority unable to close a 4% budget gap signals structural financial stress that lenders would assess as high refinancing or restructuring risk.

findings.headline: Primary care GP recruitment and sustainability challenges requiring ongoing partner investment
findings.detail: The IJMB explicitly states: 'In Primary Care there continues to be a number of continuing challenges around sustainability of some of our GP Practices with inability to recruit General Practitioners a common issue. This has necessitated the Partnership providing support and investment to maintain GP services in some parts of Moray.' This is flagged as a top financial risk with no solution articulated beyond continued 'support and investment'.
findings.matters: Inability to recruit GPs is forcing unbudgeted investment to maintain services, a cost that may grow and further strain partners. Primary care failure could cascade into higher hospital demands on the set-aside budget.
findings.figures: Unquantified but ongoing investment required to maintain GP services
findings.quote: In Primary Care there continues to be a number of continuing challenges around sustainability of some of our GP Practices with inability to recruit General Practitioners a common issue. This has necessitated the Partnership providing support and investment to maintain GP services in some parts of Moray.

findings.headline: Prescribing budget at 11% of core budget with documented volatility and unknown upside risk
findings.detail: Primary care prescribing costs are £21.392m (11% of the £192.8m core budget). The IJMB acknowledges 'prescribing costs are a large and volatile part of the MIJB budget' and has provisioned for a 'Best Prediction' scenario rather than best case. The budget notes 'Whilst the decisions to prescribe are made locally, the costs of drugs and agreements to introduce new drugs are made on a national basis,' leaving local control limited. The document flags this explicitly as a top risk.
findings.matters: Prescribing represents a significant uncontrollable budget risk; if volumes or drug costs rise above the provisioned 'best prediction', the IJMB has already exhausted its flexibility and would need additional partner funding.
findings.figures: £21.392m prescribing budget; 11% of core budget; 'volatile in nature'; specific concern about 'volume and price increases'
findings.quote: Prescribing costs are a large and volatile part of the MIJB budget with demographic changes a material contributing factor. Whilst the decisions to prescribe are made locally, the costs of drugs and agreements to introduce new drugs are made on a national basis.

findings.headline: Recurring £4.394m deficit carried forward from 2025/26 built into 2026/27 budget
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget anticipates spend includes a 'recurring deficit from 2025/26 forecast position' of £4.394m. This was flagged in the prior year as a risk: 'During 2025/26, the MIJB set a balanced budget however, risk was flagged to partners on the potential for the MIJB to deliver a deficit outturn given the scale of savings needed during the financial year.' This deficit is not being addressed but carried forward as a structural cost.
findings.matters: A recurring deficit that persists year-on-year indicates structural problems in service delivery costs that cannot be solved through one-off savings, suggesting deeper operational sustainability issues.
findings.figures: £4.394m recurring deficit carried forward; flagged in 2025/26 budget setting
findings.quote: During 2025/26, the MIJB set a balanced budget however, risk was flagged to partners on the potential for the MIJB to deliver a deficit outturn given the scale of savings needed during the financial year.

findings.headline: No general reserves held and none expected for several years
findings.detail: The MIJB holds no uncommitted general reserves and states it will not build reserves in the foreseeable future. The document confirms: 'it is unlikely it will give rise to any general reserves over the next few years'. Only £1.406m in earmarked reserves for specific programmes are expected to be exhausted by end of 2026/27. This leaves the organisation with no buffer for cost overruns or unexpected pressures.
findings.matters: Absence of reserves means any spending overspend must be absorbed by partners mid-year or result in service cuts, and indicates structural financial stress that cannot be managed internally.
findings.figures: £0 general reserves; £1.406m earmarked reserves expected to be exhausted by end 2026/27
findings.quote: With the Scheme in mind, there has only been ear marked reserves by the end of the financial year as the MIJB has not held any uncommitted general reserves for a significant period.

findings.headline: Savings plan carries high delivery risk with only 58% rated green and potential £1.074m shortfall
findings.detail: The £5.718m savings plan includes 34 proposals with risk ratings: 16 green, 14 amber, 4 red. Using conservative assumptions (green 90% delivery, amber 80%, red 70%), only £4.734m would be achieved, leaving a £1.074m gap. The document states 'it remains extremely challenging to identify additional savings to support the 2026/27 budget setting process'. Four proposals are explicitly rated red-risk including removal of locums (£450k) and review of contributions policy (£500k).
findings.matters: If the savings plan fails to deliver as projected, the MIJB and Moray Council face identifying additional unplanned reductions mid-year, likely impacting service delivery or requiring further partner funding.
findings.figures: £5.718m total savings; £4.734m likely to be achieved at RAG assumptions; £1.074m potential shortfall; 4 red-rated proposals totalling £960k
findings.quote: The savings identified are challenging to achieve fully in the year - the risk of achieving the savings has been calculated based on the RAG status, with green assuming will be 90% achieved, amber 80% and red 70% respectively. Using this assumption the savings for 2026/27 could be £4.734 million, leaving a risk of a potential funding gap, which would have to be borne by the partners of the MIJB of £1.074 million.

findings.headline: £9 million deficit funding gap to be funded by partners
findings.detail: After identifying £5.718m in savings and receiving £219m in baseline funding, the MIJB faces a £9m budget gap. This is not a projection but a formal deficit that the board is requesting partners (Moray Council and NHS Grampian) fund upfront. The budget summary shows: anticipated spend £233.766m, anticipated funding £219.048m, savings £5.718m, gap £9.000m, to be 'met by deficit funding from partners'.
findings.matters: A health and social care body requiring £9m in emergency support funding signals inability to deliver a sustainable budget and raises questions about Moray Council's ability to fund its share of this shortfall.
findings.figures: £9.000m deficit funding requirement; anticipated spend £233.766m against funding £219.048m
findings.quote: This year, given the financial gap identified after savings, and the requirement for the MIJB to set a balanced budget, contributions towards deficit support will be requested from each partner at the start of the year.

news_drafts.lead: Loss of institutional knowledge and continuity risk in asset valuation; if replacement valuer is not properly briefed or available, the 2025/26 audit and asset valuation could be delayed
